title: chore(lint): fail lint when the React Compiler skips a listed file
body: **Problem.** When the React Compiler can't prove a component or hook follows React's rules (a ref read during render, `setState` in an effect, a manual memo it can't preserve), it skips the whole function with no build error. Lint only shows a warning. `apps/web` has 369 of these skips across 91 files, so manual `useMemo`/`useCallback` still matter there, and nothing stops new code from adding more skips. **Fix.** A per-file ratchet: - An override in `vite.config.ts` lists files that must compile. In those files the compiler's bailout rules (`refs`, `set-state-in-effect`, `memo-dependencies`, `preserve-manual-memoization`, `immutability`, `purity`, ...) are errors. - The new `t3code/no-manual-memo` rule rejects `useMemo`/`useCallback` in listed files, because the compiler already memoizes them. `useStableCallback` stays allowed for the large-component handler rule in `web-ui.md`. - The list starts with `useThreadTerminalActions` and `PersistentThreadTerminals.tsx`. I removed their 16 manual memos and checked that the compiler output still memoizes both files. - Files extracted from ChatView later in this stack join the list as they land. ## Stack progress | "Crashes" means it hit an internal codegen error and left ChatView uncompiled; "skips" means it reported reasons it could not compile it. Strict files must compile with no bailouts, no manual memoization and no effect-rule violations; lint and `reactCompiledFiles.test.ts` enforce it. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) (Claude Opus 5.5) ---

files.patch:
@@ -53,3 +53,16 @@ Calls inside the component keep the plain function, so work that resumes after a
 acts on the render it started in. A function that a child calls during render, or after an
 `await`, comes from a module-level factory memoized on its inputs, so its closure keeps only
 those inputs.
+
+## React Compiler
+
+The compiler memoizes a component or hook only when it can prove the code follows React's rules.
+Anything it can't prove, such as reading a ref during render or calling `setState` from an effect,
+makes it skip the whole function without a build error. Lint reports each skip as a
+`react(...)` warning with the note "React Compiler skipped optimizing this component or hook".
+
+Files listed in the React Compiler override in [`vite.config.ts`](../../vite.config.ts) must
+compile. There those rules are errors, and `t3code/no-manual-memo` rejects `useMemo` and
+`useCallback`, which the compiler makes redundant. `useStableCallback` still marks handlers
+that leave a large component, as described above. Add a file to the list once its skips are
+fixed, and drop its manual memoization in the same change.
